title: Fix pgvector cosine operator mismatch
description:
Why: embeddings HNSW index uses vector_cosine_ops, while DrizzleRetrievalRepository.vectorScoreExpression currently scores with <=>. The audit claim is valid enough to treat as product-risk: vector search can rank with the wrong distance/operator relative to the index and intended cosine semantics.

Scope: align query operator/scoring with vector_cosine_ops semantics, update repository tests to assert generated SQL/operator behavior or a DB-backed ranking smoke if feasible, and keep embeddingModelId/dimension/finite validation intact.

Non-goals: no new eval lane, no embedding model redesign, no broad retrieval refactor.
acceptance_criteria: searchVector/searchHybrid use the operator/scoring consistent with vector_cosine_ops; focused test or DB smoke fails on the previous operator; existing retrieval substrate smoke still passes
close_reason: Rejected by evidence: official pgvector operator mapping is <-> for L2 and <=> for cosine distance; KRN index uses vector_cosine_ops and query scoring uses <=> with 1 - distance, so the audit mismatch claim is false. No code change.

title: Prove one vertical KRN product loop
description:
Why: the roadmap claims a governed loop, but the repo still lacks one deterministic proof that evidence can flow through observation/reflection/candidate/review/memory-or-source decision/activation/Codex brief/feedback and affect the next activation. Existing decision-packet eval work is useful but narrower than the full product loop.

Scope: build one tiny deterministic DB-backed product-loop scenario after source authority and public metadata are safe. The scenario should prove persisted state transitions and changed next selection, not live LLM behavior.

Non-goals: no dashboard/API/MCP, no broad benchmark suite, no live Codex claim, no prose snapshot tests, no autonomous worker daemon.
acceptance_criteria: A focused DB-backed fixture or smoke proves evidence capture -> observation -> reflection -> memory/source candidate -> review decision -> activation -> Codex brief -> feedback changes a later activation decision; every stage has persisted state assertions; failure at any stage fails the gate; output states proof and non-proof boundaries.
close_reason: Completed in e3947b8: brain-loop DB smoke now proves next-run Codex brief rendering through CLI callback, positive feedback includes helped memory in later activation, negative feedback excludes hurt memory, persisted readbacks assert every stage. Verified db/cli/harness typechecks, harness manifest test, CLI db tests, db tests, live pnpm db:smoke:brain-loop, Fallow CI, diff check, and second-opinion-claude approve LOW.

title: Make public metadata safe by default
description:
Why: public IO metadata currently starts from a permissive catchall in packages/core/src/parsing/schema-primitives.ts, while private-reasoning rejection is opt-in in selected parsers. In an AI memory system this is an authority leak: model/private reasoning keys can cross public boundaries unless each schema remembers to reject them.

Scope: introduce a safe public metadata parser or equivalent default-deny path for public IO schemas. Audit current MetadataSchema consumers in packages/core/src/parsing/*.ts and preserve explicitly internal metadata only where the boundary is named and bounded.

Non-goals: do not ban all metadata; do not rewrite unrelated schema fields; do not recreate @krn/schema; do not add prose-only tests.
acceptance_criteria: Public candidate/task/source/retrieval/evidence-facing parsers reject private-reasoning keys by default; any internal-only metadata parser is explicit in name and consumer; tests prove private reasoning keys cannot cross public candidate, source-claim, task-contract, retrieval, or evidence-capture boundaries; typecheck stays green.
close_reason: Completed. Public parser MetadataSchema now aliases PublicMetadataSchema, which rejects private-reasoning metadata keys by default while preserving arbitrary non-private metadata. Hidden reasoning aliases were folded into the same forbidden-key set. No internal metadata escape hatch was added because no current parser consumer required one. Added a focused parser-boundary test covering memory candidate, source claim, task contract, retrieval candidate, and evidence capture inputs. Applied pattern:ts-boundary-unknown-first-result-state. Verified: focused core parsing/behavior fixture tests, core typecheck, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm quality:fallow:ci, git diff --check. Claude second-opinion returned approve LOW with no findings.

title: Fix source governance blocking semantics
description:
Why: KRN's differentiator is temporal, source-backed, falsifiable authority. The audit flags source governance as the highest-risk current crack: invalid source timestamps appear to fail open, assessSourceClaimOverride may only block weaker candidates when the candidate is newer, and accepted source claims without linked decisions can read as authority instead of a blocking missing-link state.

Scope: inspect packages/core/src/source.ts and the activation/source-search/decision-packet consumers. Correct the blocking semantics for temporal invalidity, stronger-current-consensus override, and accepted-claim-without-decision inclusion. Keep this as policy behavior, not a file-splitting exercise.

Non-goals: no source taxonomy cleanup, no broad source graph redesign, no CLI rewrite, no markdown/prose tests.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid source timestamps fail closed or return an explicit invalid_time state that blocks activation authority; stronger valid consensus blocks weaker candidates independent of candidate recency unless an explicit override path is proven; accepted source claims without linked SourceDecision/SourceDecisionEdge support are blocking for activation/decision-packet authority; focused behavior tests falsify each case without snapshotting prose.
close_reason: Completed. Source governance now fails closed for invalid SourceClaim timestamps and invalid override now values; stronger accepted current consensus blocks weaker candidates independent of candidate recency; accepted SourceClaims without linked SourceDecisionEdge support are blocking review signals for activation and compileHarnessPlan authority. SourceRepository decision-edge lookup is required and wired through no-store, database runtime, eval runners, source-search, activation, compile harness, and typed CLI test fakes. Claude second-opinion: valid approve_with_fixes LOW reviewed final pre-F2 diff; F1 countered with existing newer-weaker and older-weaker source override tests; F2 accepted and fixed with invalid-now fail-closed test; F3 verified by rg call-site audit. Later invalid Claude artifact findings were handled: compiler path now has a source-review exclusion test; optional decision-edge guard removed; rg found no non-test optional decision-edge consumers. Verified: core source test, harness compiler focused test, CLI source-decision-gaps focused test, CLI typecheck:tests:clean, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm quality:fallow:ci, git diff --check.

title: Harden SourceClaim override reason semantics
description:
Why: assessSourceClaimOverride allows any non-empty overrideReason to bypass stronger current consensus. That may be intended as explicit human override, but it currently has no minimum evidence shape, no provenance requirement, and no structured audit signal. This is authority-boundary risk, not a CLI cosmetic issue.

Scope: define the smallest accepted override shape for source decisions: meaningful reason text plus explicit caller provenance or decision linkage. Add focused tests for empty/whitespace/trivial override and stronger-consensus bypass.

Non-goals: no source taxonomy rewrite, no broad consensus engine, no dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: Trivial override reasons cannot silently bypass stronger accepted consensus; legitimate explicit override remains possible with structured provenance; source tests pass

Scope: wrap database runtime factory initialization so any throw before returning a runtime closes the client exactly once. Add a focused regression test using a mocked postgres/client path or a small injectable factory if needed.

Non-goals: no pool redesign, no broad DB runtime abstraction.
acceptance_criteria: init failure after client creation closes client; success path still returns runtime with close(); existing database-runtime and DB smoke tests pass
close_reason: Completed: createDatabaseRuntime now closes the postgres client on any initialization failure before returning a runtime. Added regression for failure after project resolution. Verified CLI typecheck, focused database-runtime test, Fallow CI, and diff check.

title: Retire corpus JSON from brain runtime read path (store-backed default)
description:

Update buildProof/doesNotProve: store-backed path no longer disclaims live-DB. corpus/brain-knowledge becomes seed-only (consumed by the A3 seed command only).

title: Seed corpus patterns into memory_records (krn memory pattern seed)
description:
Why: the brain still reads retained patterns from corpus JSON files; patterns must live in the store as memory_records(kind=pattern) so the brain is DB-backed. The write path is proven (run-brain-search-db-smoke.ts creates+promotes kind=pattern via createMemoryCandidate+promoteReviewedMemoryCandidate).

Scope: new krn memory pattern seed [--file catalog.json] [--dry-run] command. Reuse parseRetainedPatternDecision (harness) to parse corpus patterns; map each RetainedPatternDecision -> CreateMemoryCandidateInput (kind=pattern, summary=name, body=decision, invalidationRule=falsifier, sourceLineage=sourceRefs, metadata={patternId,adoptionStatus,doesNotProve}); idempotently create via the proven candidate+promote path (skip if a record with key pattern:<patternId> exists). --dry-run reports without writing.

Non-goals: do not special-case pattern readback (patterns are memory cards); do not touch usefulness (that is 9xc1).

title: Rebuild the Phase-2 decision-packet falsifier to run the real engine
description:
Why: the roadmap make-or-break claim (KRN beats plain Codex + notes + grep) is currently NON-PROOF. runDecisionPacketEval and runNotesBaselineEval call rankDecisionRows(fixture.decisions, task) - a 44-LOC token-overlap scorer over static fixture rows (decisionPacketScoring.ts) - and never invoke activationEngine. The falsifier must exercise the real pipeline or every product-advantage claim is unfalsified. This is the highest-leverage gap from the audit.

Scope: replace the toy-tokenizer fixture scoring with a real end-to-end path: seed source / memory / rejection rows -> activationEngine.retrieveActivationCandidates -> assembleContext -> renderExecutionBrief; score the resulting packet against a notes-baseline on a task that contains a stale standard and a rejected path. The falsifier must be able to FAIL KRN for activating a stale or rejected path. Keep determinism (deterministicEval.test.ts must stay green). Do NOT call live Codex yet - that is a later phase; this falsifier proves the engine selects and avoids the right claims.

Non-goals: no live-Codex obedience eval in this slice; no broad benchmark lane; do not change activation scoring weights to game the eval.
acceptance_criteria: the falsifier runs retrieveActivationCandidates + assembleContext + renderExecutionBrief on seeded fixtures; it demonstrably FAILS when the engine activates a stale or rejected path; output is reproducible (deterministicEval green); at least one fixture exercises rejected-path recall and one exercises stale-standard downgrade.
notes: Verify: grep retrieveActivationCandidates in the eval runner is non-empty; runDecisionPacketEval fails on a seeded stale-path fixture. Source: kernel-direction-full-audit.
close_reason: Completed: decision-packet falsifier now runs real activation/filter/budget/context/brief engine; rankDecisionRows scorer deleted; stale/edge-boundary falsifiers verified; Claude second opinion approved after fixes.

title: eval: KRN decision packet vs Codex+notes+grep baseline
description:
Adopted from 2026-07-06 second-opinion plan (Slice 2, the make-or-break falsifier).

Why: The reviewer's weakest-claim finding is that KRN has never been compared against the realistic competitor: baseline Codex + a maintained NOTES.md + grep. If KRN cannot beat that on real task packets, the rest of the roadmap does not matter. This is executable WITHOUT live Codex (deterministic packet comparison).

Scope:
- New eval:notes-baseline. For 15-25 held-out real task framings (from recent Beads/docs/ADRs), compare the KRN decision packet (governing decisions, source refs, memories, rejected paths, non-proofs) against a curated NOTES.md+grep baseline.
- Metrics: top-k governing-decision recall, stale/noisy inclusions, missing constraints, packet size/ceremony.
- KRN must win materially (not cosmetically) on recall of governing decisions without more ceremony.
- Define the baseline precisely in the eval: what NOTES.md may contain, how grep is allowed, what 'KRN wins' means (predeclared threshold).

Acceptance:
- eval:notes-baseline runs deterministically over >=15 real framings, reports per-framing KRN-vs-notes winner + aggregate recall/noise/ceremony.
- Honest non-proof: does not prove live Codex obedience or that anyone pays.

Falsifier: notes+grep is equal or better on governing-decision recall, review burden, or setup friction. If so, STOP feature work and diagnose why KRN is not useful.

Verification: pnpm eval:notes-baseline; pnpm eval:memory-advantage; pnpm eval:brain-ranking; pnpm eval:determinism; pnpm run typecheck; pnpm test; pnpm -w run quality:fallow:ci; pnpm docs:lint; git diff --check.

Rejected: live Codex execution dependency, broad benchmark platform, cosmetic win thresholds.

title: Redefine roadmap: breakthrough product end-state + unblocked path
description:
Why this exists:
The queue keeps emptying into cleanup/investigation because the deterministic-proof phase is saturated, the live-Codex-advantage path is blocked on Codex access, and there is NO crisp actionable product end-state defined beyond the kernel mechanism (select/apply/verify/forget). When proof is done, 'what next' is undefined. This is a PLAN/ROADMAP gap, not an execution gap.

Scope (research + decision, not code):
- Define the breakthrough product end-state concretely: what does the brain DO that is more than the kernel mechanism, that an operator/team would pay for, and that is provably better than baseline Codex/RAG? Name the loop, the consumer, and the falsifier.
- Identify the UNBLOCKED paths to it (not requiring live Codex): e.g. self-fueling ingest (auto-seed real repo docs as decisions), multi-session learning within this repo, recall-quality that changes a real decision, second-opinion governed loop as a standing capability.
- Decompose the end-state into 3-6 actionable slices with acceptance + falsifier, so the queue is never empty again.
- Record as an updated PLAN / a ROADMAP decision doc.

Acceptance:
- A written decision names the breakthrough product end-state, the unblocked path, and 3-6 next slices with falsifiers.
- Each slice is something that can be done WITHOUT live Codex.

Verification: source decisions applied (docs/KRN_SOURCES pattern); bd create the resulting slices.

Proof/non-proof: makes the forward roadmap obvious and unblocked. Does not itself implement code.

Rejected directions: no live-Codex-dependent slices, no UI/API/MCP before gates, no 'do more evals' (saturated).
close_reason: Resolved by the 2026-07-06 second-opinion review. The reviewer supplied the missing crisp end-state (governed decision-packet engine: before a task select source-backed decisions/memories/constraints; after, promote/reject/downgrade/forget) and the make-or-break falsifier (beat Codex+notes+grep on real task packets, without live Codex). Verdict + plan recorded in docs/runs/2026-07-06-second-opinion-verdict-and-plan.md. Execution seeded as beads: notes-baseline (P1, the leverage slice), corpus-closure, decision-packet benchmark, feedback/forget loop, second-repo dry run. title: Senior quality pass on real-recall-advantage smoke
description:
Why this exists:
The session added runRealRecallAdvantageDbSmoke.ts under velocity. A senior review found three cleanliness issues that must be fixed before calling the code breakthrough-quality: (1) an unnecessary close/reopen of the database runtime between seed phases - queries inject their own runtime via bindSmokeProjectRuntimeFactory, so one runtime can cover all seeding; (2) an 'as Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createDatabaseRuntime>>' cast that papers over a let-captured-undefined instead of using a local const; (3) a Fallow duplication warn on the createSourceClaim block shared by seedDecision and seedDistractor.

Scope:
- Hold ONE runtime across distractor + governing seeding; remove the second createDatabaseRuntime(projectId) call and the intermediate close/reopen.
- Remove the cast by using a local const for the seeding runtime.
- Extract createSmokeSourceClaim helper to clear the Fallow warn (gate should report 0 duplication, not warn).
- Keep behavior identical: smoke still proves 3/3 distractor-competition advantage, reproducible.

Acceptance criteria:
- Smoke still passes 3/3 after refactor (reproducible).
- pnpm run typecheck clean; pnpm -w run quality:fallow:ci exit 0 with NO duplication warn-line on this file.
- No new cast or any-cast introduced.

Verification:
- pnpm db:smoke:real-recall-advantage (3/3, twice)
- pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- db.test
- pnpm run typecheck
- pnpm -w run quality:fallow:ci
- git diff --check

Proof/non-proof:
Proves the smoke is senior-clean (no runtime thrash, no casts, no duplication). Does not change the proof's meaning or coverage.

Rejected directions:
No behavior change, no new coverage, no rename of the smoke target.
close_reason: Completed: senior quality pass on runRealRecallAdvantageDbSmoke.ts. (1) Removed the unnecessary close/reopen dance - one seeding runtime now covers distractor + governing seed phases (recall queries inject their own runtime via bindSmokeProjectRuntimeFactory). (2) Removed the 'as Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createDatabaseRuntime>>' cast by using a local const seedingRuntime. (3) Eliminated the Fallow duplication warns by unifying seedDecision + seedDistractor into a single seedRealRecallClaim driven by a RealRecallSeedVariant descriptor (governing vs distractor as data, not parallel functions). Behavior identical. Verification: pnpm db:smoke:real-recall-advantage 3/3 (run twice, reproducible); pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- db.test (399 passed); pnpm run typecheck; pnpm -w run quality:fallow:ci (exit 0, NO duplication/dead-code lines - fully clean, not warn); pnpm docs:lint; git diff --check.

title: Close brain blindness gap: adopt real governing decisions
description:
Why this exists:
The 2026-07-05 live dogfood (mise-en-palace-y7yg) found that ~11/23 persistent real source claims have no SourceDecisionEdge and are therefore invisible to source-search. The brain's effective recallable knowledge (12) is roughly half its raw claim corpus (23). Closing this gap is the highest-leverage immediate gain: it directly fixes the blindness the dogfood exposed.

Scope:
- Enumerate the 11 un-edged real claims and classify each as (a) a real KRN governing decision worth adopting vs (b) a multi-repo/dogfood leftover (EKOLOGUS target-repo content, V338/V339/V342 proved-*, IMR heartbeat) that must NOT be promoted to an adopted decision.
- Adopt + link ONLY the real governing decisions via the product CLI (krn source decision adopt --persist + krn source decision link --persist). Candidates include: ADR-0021 temporal source relations claims, the retained-KRN-knowledge gate claim, the bounded-local-artifact-flow claim.
- Re-run the dogfood queries that missed (dashboard already fixed in slice 3; temporal source relations) and prove the temporal-relation decision now surfaces.
- Report effective-knowledge before/after (claims-with-edge count).

Acceptance criteria:
- >=3 real governing decisions adopted + linked via product commands (not DB-hack).
- The temporal-relations query surfaces an ADR-0021 claim after teaching where it was absent before.
- Run doc records before/after with honest classification of which claims were adopted vs deliberately left as dogfood leftovery.
- No EKOLOGUS/proved-*/heartbeat claims adopted as governing decisions.

Verification:
- pnpm db:ready
- krn source decision adopt/link --persist (per claim)
- krn source search --json before/after
- pnpm docs:lint
- git diff --check

Proof/non-proof:
Proves the brain's effective recallable knowledge rises and the teach loop scales beyond one claim. Does not prove recall is now perfect, that all adopted decisions are correctly worded, live Codex adherence, or broad ranking quality.

Rejected directions:
No DB-hacking (product CLI only), no adopting dogfood/multi-repo leftover claims as governing decisions, no claim that 23/23 is the right target.
close_reason: Completed: classified the 11 un-edged real claims and adopted the 4 real KRN governing decisions via product CLI (adopt+link): temporal-relations-as-SourceClaimEdge (ADR-0021), second-bounded-artifact-flow-before-surfaces, retained-knowledge gate, temporal-edge semantics. Deliberately skipped 7 dogfood/multi-repo/trial leftovery (EKOLOGUS, V338/V339/V342/V371 proved-*, generic preview claim, duplicate) - not governing standards. Effective knowledge: claims-with-edge 13->17 (12->17 across slice 3+4). Verification: temporal query now surfaces ADR-0021 claims at rank 1+2 (was absent); retained-knowledge query surfaces gate at rank 1 (was absent). Run doc: docs/runs/2026-07-05-close-blindness-gap-adopt-real-decisions.md. Boundary: 6 real claims remain un-edged by design; diagnostic under-reporting is slice 5 (9tzh); rank-quality is slice 6 (1nk1). Verification: pnpm db:ready; krn source decision adopt/link --persist; krn source search --json before/after; pnpm docs:lint; git diff --check.

title: Live-dogfood brain recall and teach the real gap
description:
Why this exists:
Slice 1/2 proved recall and distractor-competition advantage deterministically. Slice 3 is the live dogfood: actually USE the brain (krn source search) on real task framings against the persistent real-claim corpus, observe where it recalls well and where it misses, then use the brain's own product commands (krn source decision gaps/adopt/link) to teach the missed governing decision and prove recall improves.

Scope:
- Run krn source search for >=5 real task framings (MCP/API exposure, dashboard, temporal relations, valid retained pattern, Memory Core mutation) against the persistent real-claim DB.
- Run krn source decision gaps to diagnose which accepted real claims lack SourceDecisionEdge support (invisible to source-search).
- For at least one missed real governing decision (e.g. bounded-local-loop before crawler/dashboard/API), adopt + link it via the product commands so it becomes recallable.
- Re-run the query and prove the brain now surfaces it.
- Record the full loop (recall -> diagnose -> teach -> recall improves) in a docs/runs run doc with honest findings, including that claims without SourceDecisionEdge are invisible to source-search (the slice-2 finding, now confirmed on persistent real content).

Acceptance criteria:
- Run doc records >=5 live queries with their top results, distinguishing recalled-vs-missed governing decisions.
- source decision gaps output captured as the diagnostic.
- At least one missed real decision adopted+linked via product commands and shown to surface after teaching (before/after query output).
- Honest non-proof: dogfood is operator-driven on a curated persistent corpus, not a live Codex loop or broad recall-quality benchmark.

Verification:
- pnpm db:ready
- krn source decision gaps
- krn source decision adopt --persist / krn source decision link --persist
- krn source search --json before/after

title: Prove real recall advantage beats lexically-stronger distractors
description:
Why this exists:
Slice 1 (mise-en-palace-b8xl) proved natural-language recall works on real repo decisions through the live architecture, but its baseline was an isolated empty project - honest but weak. It did not prove ADVANTAGE over a real competitor. Slice 2 makes the baseline a lexically-stronger distractor: a tempting-but-wrong shortcut seeded without a SourceDecisionEdge, so pure lexical retrieval picks it first, while the brain's decision-linked recall (SourceDecisionEdge boost) surfaces the governing decision ahead of it.

Scope:
- Extend db:smoke:real-recall-advantage: each of the 3 real decisions gets a distractor claim (plausible wrong shortcut, high lexical overlap, accepted but NO SourceDecision/SourceDecisionEdge).
- Baseline pass: seed ONLY distractors; run each natural-language query; assert the distractor is the top candidate (brain without the governing decision picks the wrong shortcut).
- Grounded pass: also seed the governing decisions WITH SourceDecisionEdge; run queries; assert the governing claim is now the top candidate (decision-linked recall overrules the lexically-stronger distractor).
- Report per-case: baselineTopClaimId, groundedTopClaimId, advantageWin (baseline=distractor AND grounded=governing), plus aggregate advantageWinCount.
- Update behavior-gate-matrix.md row to reflect distractor-competition advantage.

Acceptance criteria:
- >=2 of 3 cases classify as advantageWin (baseline picks distractor, grounded picks governing) on the live DB via the real source-search path.
- Output reports per-case baseline/grounded top claim ids and an honest non-proof (decision-edge boost magnitude is fixture-tuned, not a general ranking-quality proof).

Verification:
- pnpm db:ready
- pnpm db:smoke:real-recall-advantage (reproducible)
- pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- db.test
- pnpm run typecheck
- pnpm -w run quality:fallow:ci
- pnpm docs:lint
- git diff --check

Proof/non-proof:
Proves the brain's decision-linked recall preferentially surfaces accepted governing decisions over lexically-stronger unlinked distractors on the live DB. Does not prove the boost generalizes to arbitrary lexical gaps, live Codex adherence, broad ranking quality, or that every real task is covered.

Rejected directions:
No live Codex execution dependency, no in-memory-only proof, no new smoke file (extend the existing real-recall-advantage lane), no benchmark platform.
close_reason: Completed slice 2 of the fixture->real arc: db:smoke:real-recall-advantage now proves honest distractor-competition advantage on the live DB. Each of 3 real governing decisions gets a tempting-but-wrong distractor (accepted SourceClaim + LOW-confidence SourceDecisionEdge + lexically-dense SearchDocument). Baseline pass seeds ONLY distractors and proves each natural-language query picks the distractor as top recall result (brain without the governing decision picks the shortcut) - 3/3 baseline distractor tops. Grounded pass also seeds the governing decision (HIGH-confidence SourceDecisionEdge) and proves the governing claim becomes the top result because decision-linked confidence overrules the lexically-stronger distractor - 3/3 grounded governing tops. Advantage wins: 3/3 (>= majority threshold). Reproducible across runs. Key finding during build: source-search does NOT surface SourceClaims lacking a SourceDecisionEdge (0 candidates), so the distractor must carry a LOW-confidence edge to be visible; the governing HIGH-confidence edge then beats it. Refactor: extracted createSmokeSourceArtifact helper (Fallow exit 0; one remaining createSourceClaim clone is a warn, below the error threshold). Updated behavior-gate-matrix.md row. Honest boundary: proves decision-linked confidence recall beats a lexically-stronger low-confidence distractor on real repo decisions via the live architecture. Does NOT prove the confidence boost generalizes to arbitrary lexical gaps, live Codex adherence, broad ranking quality, or full task coverage.

title: Resolve DecisionPacket naming void: name the product type OR retire the roadmap term
description:
OPERATOR DECISION. Why: the roadmap names DecisionPacket as the operator-facing product (line 45) and a target type (line 522), but NO DecisionPacket type exists in @krn/core or @krn/harness (grep for interface/type/class DecisionPacket in core/harness = ZERO; only CLI eval fixtures use the name). The real product is split across three names: ContextAssembly (core/contextAssembly.ts), ExecutionBrief (codex-adapter/renderExecutionBrief.ts), and RunReadbackResource (cli/runShowReadback.ts, 1098 LOC, the de-facto read model). A new agent reading the roadmap then the code cannot map DecisionPacket to any single type. Phase 2 (Decision-Packet Falsifier) has no named target.

Scope: operator picks ONE. (a) Introduce a thin DecisionPacket type in @krn/core composing the already-built ContextAssembly + ExecutionBrief pair, and rename runShowReadback RunReadbackResource to DecisionPacketReadModel (file decisionPacketReadModel.ts); the build/render pair becomes buildDecisionPacket / renderDecisionPacket; keep the CLI verb run show only on the command file. OR (b) edit KRN_ROADMAP.md (lines 45 and 521-531) to retire DecisionPacket in favor of the implemented names. Either branch removes the doc/code drift.

Non-goals: do not change ContextAssembly/ExecutionBrief structure or activation behavior (naming/type-composition only); no batch rename of the 33 run*Command files; do not move runShowReadback out of CLI in this slice (FromMetadata relocation is C3).
acceptance_criteria: If (a): a DecisionPacket type exists in @krn/core, RunReadbackResource renamed to DecisionPacketReadModel, the roadmap term maps to a real type. If (b): KRN_ROADMAP.md edited so no term names a non-existent type. Either way a reader can map the roadmap product name to exactly one code type (or zero, deliberately retired). typecheck + test + decision-packet eval green.
notes: Depends on C3 (FromMetadata relocation) so the read model rename lands on a clean decode layer. Source: kernel-direction-full-audit.

title: Decide and execute workers package boundary (plnv / g1gk)
description:
OPERATOR DECISION. Why: @krn/workers is honestly scoped as contract/preview-only (README: requiresBackgroundLoop false; no daemon, executor, or loop), verified at 2063 LOC across 5 HeartbeatPreview files + 2 contract files. But the naming pre-commits to Layer-6 maintenance-runtime vocabulary (Heartbeat implies a running scheduler) that the roadmap has NOT committed to build (Phase 6 explicitly defers: decide whether workers are real executors or contract/readback helpers). The CLI surface (heartbeatPreviewReadback.ts, runHeartbeatPreviewCommand) inherits the false-authority name. This is the roadmap non-goal: no package pretends to enforce a boundary it only describes.

Scope: operator picks ONE. (a) Rename @krn/workers to @krn/maintenance-preview; rename the HeartbeatPreview files to MaintenanceCandidateProposal / ConsensusEvaluationContract / KnowledgeAcquisitionContract (remove Heartbeat entirely); shrink the CLI heartbeat-preview surface accordingly. OR (b) delete @krn/workers and relocate the preview functions into @krn/cli where other readback/preview code lives, deleting the heartbeat-preview CLI command. Execute the chosen branch as a focused slice.

Non-goals: do not build a worker daemon/executor/loop (deferred to P6); do not rename in isolation if plnv resolves to delete.
acceptance_criteria: operator picks (a) or (b). If (a): package renamed, all Heartbeat names gone, README still honest about non-runtime. If (b): packages/workers deleted, previews relocated, CLI heartbeat-preview command removed. Either way no file asserts runtime authority the code disclaims; typecheck + test + build green; g1gk and plnv closed with the decision recorded.
notes: Note: the plnv framing "dead runtime preview package" is imprecise - workers is a LIVE contract package with misleading naming, not dead code. Source: kernel-direction-full-audit.

title: Move FromMetadata deserializers out of @krn/core into the persistence/decode layer
description:

The FromMetadata suffix advertises the storage shape inside the domain package. This is exactly the pattern AGENTS.md forbids: from X to Y conversion names that expose storage plumbing to product code. The CLI (runShowReadback.ts) then re-reads the same metadata a third time. Must land before the feedback fork fix (9xc1) so the unified read model has a clean home.

Scope: move the 4 functions to @krn/db mappers (or a CLI decode module) and rename to buildTargetEvidence, buildSourceUsefulnessOutcomes, buildPatternUsefulnessOutcomes, buildActivationRetrievalDiagnostics operating on validated input. Update callers (runShowReadback.ts, reviewDomain.test.ts, evidenceBundle.test.ts, krnBehaviorGate.ts). Keep the domain TYPES in core; only deserialization moves. Do NOT move the runShowReadback-local FromMetadata funcs (projectResolutionFromMetadata etc.) yet - those move with the DecisionPacket naming decision (D2).

Non-goals: do not change metadata schema or keys (that is a migration); do not unify the feedback fork here (that is 9xc1).
acceptance_criteria: grep for FromMetadata under packages/core/src returns ZERO; the builders live in the decode layer on validated input; all callers updated; pnpm typecheck + pnpm test green; Fallow reports no orphaned imports.
notes:
Unblocks 9xc1 and D2. Source: kernel-direction-full-audit.
RE-SCOPE (session 2026-07-06): folded into mise-en-palace-9xc1. The 3 core FromMetadata functions (sourceUsefulnessOutcomesFromMetadata, patternUsefulnessOutcomesFromMetadata, targetEvidenceFromMetadata) are cohesive with their core-local helpers (sourceUsefulnessOutcomeField, normalizeTargetEvidence, targetChangedFilesField) and patternUsefulnessOutcomesFromMetadata is exactly what 9xc1 rewrites anyway. Moving them separately would double-touch + invert layering. The FromMetadata rename will happen as part of 9xc1 when it reshapes the decoder. Closed-as-folded; no standalone work.
close_reason: Folded into 9xc1 (see notes): standalone FromMetadata move would double-touch code 9xc1 rewrites and drag core-local helpers. Rename lands with 9xc1.

title: Decide outbox substrate: wire a consumer OR delete it
description:
Why: DrizzleOutboxRepository (enqueue + listPending only) and DrizzleEventLedgerRepository (appendRunEvent) appear to be write-only primitives with no runtime consumer. If nothing drains the outbox, it is speculative surface violating the roadmap rule: no subsystem without a runtime consumer.

Scope: audit every enqueue / listPending / appendRunEvent call site (grep for listPending, enqueue, outbox, appendRunEvent under packages, excluding schema and tests). If a real consumer exists, document it. If none exists, delete DrizzleOutboxRepository (and DrizzleEventLedgerRepository if likewise write-only), the table schema, and the migration that adds the table, after confirming nothing reads them. This is evidence-driven: the answer follows from the call-site audit, not a product preference.

Non-goals: do not build a worker daemon to drain the outbox (roadmap defers the maintenance runtime to P6).
acceptance_criteria: Either the outbox has a documented runtime consumer; or DrizzleOutboxRepository and its table are deleted with typecheck + test green and no dangling references. No write-only primitive remains.
notes: Source: kernel-direction-full-audit.
close_reason: No-op after evidence: the outbox is NOT dead. DrizzleHarnessRunRepository inserts outbox_events in-transaction with writes; doctorStaticChecks reads it; smokes count by feedbackDeltaId. It is a live transactional event log. Only listPending lacks a product drainer, which is intentional (deferred to P6 maintenance runtime). Deleting it would break feedback/harness-run event emission. No code change warranted.

title: Move brain usefulness feedback from JSON corpus to store-backed events
description: Why: usefulness feedback is runtime/event evidence, not a permanent JSON ledger. Current cleanup removed active usefulness-feedback files from corpus. Scope: design or reuse DB/event tables for pattern usefulness feedback, query it through read models, and keep corpus JSON as bootstrap fixtures only. Acceptance: brain knowledge readback can show usefulness outcome from store-backed events; no docs or static JSON ledger is required for current usefulness; tests prove no-feedback and helped-feedback paths.
notes:
RE-SCOPE (kernel-direction-full-audit, 2026-07-06): the revert was for execution defects (alias-only rename, missing tests, hardcoded slugs, undocumented outcome semantics), NOT wrong direction. The fork is real and this remains the highest-value fix. Re-attempt with these refinements: (1) BrainKnowledgeUsefulnessFeedback becomes a READ MODEL over FeedbackDelta store events, not a parallel JSON structure - same type, same store path; corpus/brain-knowledge JSON becomes seed-only. (2) PROVE THE READ SIDE: memory_feedback_events and observation_feedback_events are currently write-only in product code (inserted, never read by a read model) - this slice must implement the read model that reads usefulness from those events, not just add more writes. (3) feedback ingestion must join on ActivationTrace (retrievalRunId / contextAssemblyId) so "did the included standard help" is answerable. (4) Tests for helped / no-feedback / unused / stale paths. (5) Document outcome-value semantics (7 values today: selected|used|helped|neutral|noise|stale|unknown, all funnel through one field). (6) No hardcoded workspaceSlug / projectSlug. PRECONDITIONS: land C2 (slug consolidation = mise-en-palace-48f9) and C3 (FromMetadata relocation = mise-en-palace-is6c) first so the unification is real and does not re-introduce the reverted defects. Dependencies wired: 9xc1 now blocked-by 48f9 and is6c.
DESIGN LOCK (session 2026-07-06, post-investigation):
Two usefulness concepts today: (1) feedback-delta usefulness in feedback_delta.metadata JSON (run-show path, ALREADY store-backed); (2) brain-knowledge usefulness read from CORPUS JSON by brain-knowledge-read-model.ts:443.
GAP = #2: brain-knowledge pattern usefulness must be read from the STORE (feedback_delta records carrying patternUsefulnessOutcomes), not corpus JSON; corpus becomes seed-only.
KEY DECISION NEEDED: align the enums - SourceUsefulnessOutcome (7: selected|used|helped|neutral|noise|stale|unknown) vs memoryApplicationOutcome (4: helped|hurt|neutral|stale). This is the exact semantic gap that caused the prior revert. Recommend: document the 7->4 mapping explicitly OR extend memoryApplicationOutcome to match, with a per-outcome feedback-event handler.
Implementation shape: (a) give brain-knowledge-read-model a feedback-repository dependency to query feedback_deltas by patternId; (b) build usefulness readback from store records; (c) corpus JSON -> seed-only; (d) falsifier tests for no-feedback/helped/unused/stale; (e) run second-opinion-claude (CLAUDE.md mandates for migration slices).
Preconditions already met: C2 slug consolidation done (commit e9b68a3d); run-readback split (commit 1674dba3) isolates the decoders this touches.

title: Harden smoke createId uniqueness across both DB smokes
description:
Why this exists:
The session review flagged a latent przypał: createId in runRealRecallAdvantageDbSmoke is ${prefix}-${smokeId} and is shared across the 6 recall passes, so the task/intent ids handed to runSourceSearchCommand collide. Harmless today (retrieveActivationCandidates is read-only) but a landmine if source-search ever persists. The same pattern exists in runBrainSearchDbSmoke. The project bar is zero przypałów.

Scope:
- Make createId produce unique ids per call in both smokes (e.g., fold in a monotonic counter or the decision.id / phase), so task/intent ids never collide across passes.
- Keep determinism of marker cleanup (which keys on smokeId/source, not id values).
- Both smokes still pass reproducibly.

Acceptance criteria:
- createId returns distinct values across all calls within a smoke run.
- Both smokes pass reproducibly (3/3 real-recall; brain-search green).
- No test asserts a specific id string value that would now break.

Verification:
- pnpm db:smoke:real-recall-advantage (3/3, twice)
- pnpm db:smoke:brain-search
- pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- db.test
- pnpm run typecheck
- pnpm -w run quality:fallow:ci
- git diff --check

Proof/non-proof:
Proves the smokes have no latent id-collision. Does not change proof semantics.

Rejected directions:
No UUID generation (needs randomness/determinism), no changing the seeded claim id format if avoidable.
close_reason: Completed: closed the latent id-collision przypal from the session review. Added createUniqueSmokeCreateId(smokeId) to smokeRuntimeCleanup.ts - a counter-based createId factory that returns ${prefix}-${smokeId}-${counter++}, so every generated id is unique per call. Replaced the non-unique ${prefix}-${smokeId} createId in runRealRecallAdvantageDbSmoke (inline) and runBrainSearchDbSmoke (local createSmokeId helper) with the shared factory. Counter is deterministic under sequential code; unique across concurrent recall passes that share one closure. Marker cleanup/count unaffected (key on smokeId/source, not id values). Both smokes still pass reproducibly: real-recall 3/3 (run twice), brain-search green. title: Live dogfood at scale: brain informs a real implementation task
description:

This slice records a fuller live dogfood: while implementing a real repo task (the adopt --link command from the sibling bead), query the brain (krn source search + krn source decision gaps) BEFORE and DURING implementation, and document which governing decisions surfaced and how they shaped the work.

Scope:

- git diff --check

Proves the brain can inform real implementation work via its own CLI on a real task. Does not prove live Codex adherence, broad advantage, or that every task benefits.

No staged/fake task, no claim the brain is always right, no benchmark.

title: Prove memory changes real engineering implementation decisions
description:

description:

description:

title: Recall-quality: investigate why governing decisions rank below lexically-stronger peers
description: Seed for later. The slice-3 dogfood showed that even after teaching, the bounded-loop governing decision reached rank 3 (not 1) for the dashboard query - lexically-stronger claims still outranked it. Investigate the source-search ranking composition (lexical vs vector vs SourceDecisionEdge confidence/support boost) and propose a bounded, honest tuning so high-confidence governing decisions surface at rank 1 for clearly-governing queries, without breaking distractor-competition (slice 2). Not started in this session; scoped when reached.
close_reason: Investigated, no safe clean win - closed by evidence. Empirical finding: for the dashboard query, ALL included candidates tie at totalScore=95 (lexicalScore=40, graphScore=25). The bounded-loop governing decision ranks last purely due to arbitrary tie-break (DB row order), NOT because it is less relevant. The candidates are genuinely tied. Forcing rank-1 via a subjective tiebreak (raw lexical hit count, confidence, etc.) would be fixture-fitting, not senior, and risks breaking slice 2's distractor-competition proof (which relies on the current score composition where high-confidence governing beats low-confidence distractor). The real recall gap was the missing-edge blindness (fixed in slices 4/5), not ranking quality. Recall works: the governing decision IS surfaced in top-k. Rank-position for genuinely-tied candidates is not a defect. No code change shipped. Honest outcome: investigated, ranking is defensible as-is.
